Select GWR predictors by forward selection on AICc

Source: R/model-selection-gwr.R
gwr_model_selection.Rd

Grows a GWR model one predictor at a time and scores every intermediate model with a corrected Akaike information criterion, the sweep GWmodel::gwr.model.selection() defines, and returns a ranked table with each model's distance from the best. The model without predictors is scored too. Every model is fitted by the package's own local solve (see "The local solve" in fit_gwr_model), so a candidate that is constant inside some windows, a regional indicator say, is scored on what those windows do estimate and neither stops the sweep nor scores as rounding error.

Usage

gwr_model_selection(
  data_sf,
  response_var,
  candidate_vars,
  bandwidth = NULL,
  adaptive = TRUE,
  kernel = c("bisquare", "gaussian", "tricube", "boxcar", "exponential"),
  bw_approach = c("AICc", "CV"),
  max_models = 200L,
  dmat_max_n = 2000L,
  quiet = TRUE,
  .engine = .gwr_ms_engine
)

# S3 method for class 'gwr_model_selection'
print(x, n = 10L, ...)

Arguments

data_sf

An sf object with response, predictors and geometry.

response_var

Response column name.

candidate_vars

Character vector naming at least two numeric predictors to choose among. Factor, character and logical candidates are refused: a factor is several model-matrix columns while this sweep counts it as one variable, so the criteria would not be comparable, and fit_gwr_model(), the documented next step, takes only numerics. Encode them as numeric indicators first.

bandwidth

Bandwidth held fixed across all candidate models. If NULL (default) it is searched for on the model containing every candidate, by the grid-then-refine search of fit_gwr_model() (see its Bandwidth selection); what the search scored is returned in bandwidth_search. Integer neighbour count when adaptive = TRUE; otherwise a distance in the units of the projected CRS the sweep runs in, which prep_model_data() may have chosen for you. Geographic input is projected before the bandwidth is used, so a value in degrees would be read as metres; a fixed bandwidth below a ten-thousandth of the data's extent raises a warning saying so, as in fit_gwr_model(). An adaptive count too small for the full model is raised, with a warning, to the number of candidates plus 3 for the bisquare and tricube kernels (which give the farthest neighbour in a window weight 0), plus 2 for the others. That floor is enough unless several neighbours tie at the kernel's edge (a regular grid), which leaves a window fewer weighted points; then use a larger bandwidth. An adaptive count below 1 or above R's largest integer is refused, as in fit_gwr_model(). One above the number of observations is capped at it, with a warning.

adaptive

Logical; adaptive (nearest-neighbour) bandwidth. Default TRUE.

kernel

Weighting kernel: one of "bisquare" (default), "gaussian", "tricube", "boxcar" or "exponential", as in fit_gwr_model().

bw_approach

Criterion for the bandwidth search on the full model: "AICc" (default, the criterion fit_gwr_model() uses) or "CV", the leave-one-out sum of squared prediction errors. fit_gwr_model() has no CV option, so with "CV" pass the selected bandwidth to it explicitly. When observations share a location the search leaves out whole locations whichever is asked for; see Observations that share a location.

max_models

Refuse the call if the sweep would exceed this many model fits. Default 200, which admits up to 19 candidates.

dmat_max_n

Not used. The sweep takes its distances window by window and builds no n x n distance matrix, so a fixed bandwidth works at any n. The argument is accepted so that calls written with it run.

quiet

Print no progress. Default TRUE, unlike select_features_forward(). With FALSE one line is written (with cat()) as each model is fitted, to watch a long sweep progress.

.engine

Internal; leave at the default.

x

A gwr_model_selection object.

n

Number of top-ranked models print() shows. Default 10.

...

Not used.

Value

An object of class gwr_model_selection, a list with:

best

Character vector of the selected predictors, the model with the lowest criterion; character(0) when that is the model without predictors.

table

Ranked data.frame of every model evaluated, with columns rank, n_vars, variables, criterion and delta, the criterion minus the best model's. The model without predictors is the row <none>. criterion is NA, and the model is ranked last, where it could not be evaluated or where AICc is undefined because the model's effective number of parameters \(tr(S)\) is not below \(n - 2\) (with a warning).

within_2, smallest_within_2

The rows of table whose delta is at most 2, and the predictors of the smallest model among them.

criterion

"AICc".

criterion_by_name, criterion_column, criterion_verified

Where the criterion was read from the diagnostic table: TRUE, 3 and TRUE with the built-in engine.

response_var, candidate_vars

The response and the full candidate set the sweep ran over, both echoed by print().

bandwidth, bandwidth_source, adaptive, kernel

The smoothing held fixed across the sweep, and where it came from: "supplied", or the criterion's name followed by "search on the full model", the criterion being "leave-one-location-out CV" when observations share a location.

bandwidth_search

What the search scored, as fit_gwr_model keeps it; NULL when the bandwidth was supplied.

n_obs, n_models

The number of observations, and the number of rows of table.

used_dmat

Always FALSE.

raw

The forward sweep in the layout GWmodel::gwr.model.selection() returns: the two-element list of its model list and its diagnostic table, without the model that has no predictors.

Scope of the criterion

AICc penalises the effective number of parameters but is computed on the data the model was fitted to, and under spatial autocorrelation an in-sample criterion is optimistic in a way that a spatially blocked estimate is not. Use this function as a fast screen and confirm with select_features_forward(), which runs the same forward search on a spatially blocked cross-validated score at a higher cost.

Every model is fitted at one bandwidth, as Lu et al. (2014) define the method: comparing criteria across models needs the smoothing held fixed. The bandwidth chosen for the full model is not optimal for smaller ones, so refit the selected model with bandwidth = NULL once the set is settled.

The model without predictors, and the gaps

The forward sweep starts from one predictor, so by itself it always names at least one, whether or not any candidate helps. The model without predictors, a local mean at the sweep's bandwidth, is therefore scored as well and ranked with the others as <none>. When it ranks first, best is character(0): no candidate improves on it.

The delta column of table is each model's criterion minus the best one's. Differences of AICc below about 2 do not separate two models (Burnham and Anderson 2002), so within_2 lists the models that close to the best and smallest_within_2 names the one among them with the fewest predictors, which is the one to prefer when several are that close. best is still the model with the lowest criterion.

Observations that share a location

When rows of data_sf have the same coordinates, the bandwidth search leaves out whole locations, for either bw_approach (see fit_gwr_model, Observations that share a location); bandwidth_source then reads "leave-one-location-out CV search on the full model". The models are still ranked by AICc, which counts the rows at one location as independent, so the gaps overstate what a predictor adds when a location has an effect of its own; a warning of class "spatialkit_gwr_repeated_locations" says so with the counts. A model whose fit reproduces the mean of the observations at each location (every such model scores the same, whatever its predictors) has criterion NA and is listed last, as is one with a term that no local window can estimate; a warning names them.

Cost

The sweep fits p * (p + 1) / 2 GWR models for p candidates (55 at p = 10, 210 at p = 20), and the one without predictors, each over all n locations. max_models stops the call before it runs for hours.

Using $raw with GWmodel directly

raw has the layout of GWmodel's own list(model.list, GWR.df), so its two elements have to be unpacked before GWmodel's helpers will take them: GWmodel::gwr.model.view() takes (DeVar, InDeVars, model.list), so the call is


  GWmodel::gwr.model.view(sel$response_var, sel$candidate_vars, sel$raw[[1]])

Pass sel$raw[[1]], not sel$raw. The diagnostic table is sel$raw[[2]], a numeric matrix whose columns are bandwidth, AIC, AICc, RSS in that order (and are named so); the criterion column of $table is its third column.

Printing

print() shows the response, the candidate predictors, and the top-ranked models with their criterion values and, in the delta column, how far each is from the best. Below the table it lists the models within 2 of the best, which a difference in AICc does not separate (Burnham and Anderson 2002), and names the smallest of them. When several models are that close, treat the choice of predictors as unsettled; when the model without predictors (<none>) is among them, no candidate has been shown to help. print() returns x invisibly.

References

Burnham, K. P. and Anderson, D. R. (2002). Model Selection and Multimodel Inference: A Practical Information-Theoretic Approach, 2nd edition. Springer.

Lu, B., Harris, P., Charlton, M. and Brunsdon, C. (2014). The GWmodel R package: further topics for exploring spatial heterogeneity using geographically weighted models. Geo-spatial Information Science 17(2), 85–101. doi:10.1080/10095020.2014.917453

See also

select_features_forward() for the blocked cross-validated counterpart, plot.gwr_model_selection() to draw the models, and fit_gwr_model() to fit the selected model.

Other predictor selection: plot.feature_selection(), plot.gwr_model_selection(), select_features_forward()

Examples

library(sf)
set.seed(1)
n <- 80
dat <- st_as_sf(
  data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 1000),
             a = rnorm(n), b = rnorm(n), noise = rnorm(n)),
  coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632
)
# The slope on a rises from 1 in the west to 3 in the east.
east <- (st_coordinates(dat)[, 1] - 5e5) / 1000
dat$z <- (1 + 2 * east) * dat$a - dat$b + rnorm(n, 0, 0.3)
sel <- gwr_model_selection(dat, "z", c("a", "b", "noise"), bandwidth = 30)
sel                     # every model tried, by AICc, with the gaps
#> Geographically weighted regression - forward model selection
#> 
#>   response    : z
#>   candidates  : 3 (a, b, noise)
#>   observations: 80
#>   models      : 7
#>   bandwidth   : 30 (adaptive; supplied)
#>   kernel      : bisquare
#>   criterion   : AICc
#> 
#>  rank n_vars     variables criterion     delta
#>     1      2         a + b  70.55026   0.00000
#>     2      3 a + b + noise  81.27942  10.72916
#>     3      1             a 262.02384 191.47358
#>     4      2     a + noise 268.26330 197.71304
#>     5      1             b 371.33475 300.78449
#>     6      0        <none> 374.24430 303.69404
#>     7      1         noise 384.67142 314.12116
#> 
#> Selected: z ~ a + b
#> 
#> No other model is within 2 of the best; the runner-up is 10.73 away.
#> 
#> The criterion is in-sample and every model shares one bandwidth.
#> Confirm with select_features_forward() before relying on this.
sel$best                # the winning predictor set
#> [1] "a" "b"
# Refit with the bandwidth chosen afresh for the selected set.
fit_gwr_model(dat, "z", sel$best)
#> <GWR> spatial model fit
#>   Formula : z ~ a + b
#>   n       : 80
#>   CRS     : EPSG:32632
#>   Bandwidth: 35 neighbours (adaptive, bisquare kernel)
#>   AICc    : 70.30
#>   Eff. parameters: 22.0 of 80 observations
